trades.name: Electrical Installation
trades.tagline: Wiring, testing and maintaining safe electrical systems.

tools.name: Wire Strippers
tools.short: Shaped notches cut insulation without nicking the copper.
tools.what: Wire strippers have shaped notches sized to different cable diameters, gripping and cutting through insulation without nicking the copper conductor underneath.
tools.usage: Electricians use them to remove an exact length of insulation before connecting or terminating a cable — a clean strip makes for a safer, more reliable connection.

parts.label: Notched jaws
parts.body: Graduated notches match common cable sizes, cutting the insulation cleanly without damaging the wire.

parts.label: Pivot
parts.body: The pivot point lets the two handles scissor together to close the jaws with force.

parts.label: Handle grips
parts.body: Moulded grips give a comfortable, secure hold for repeated stripping and cutting.

quiz.q: What are wire strippers designed to avoid damaging?
Why does a clean, precise strip matter?
options: For a safe, reliable electrical connection

tools.name: Multimeter
tools.short: Measures voltage, current and resistance in a circuit.
tools.what: A multimeter measures voltage, current and resistance, letting you test whether a circuit is live, broken, or working correctly.
tools.usage: Electricians use it constantly — to prove a circuit is dead before working on it, diagnose faults, and check the continuity of wiring.

parts.label: Display
parts.body: Shows the live reading — volts, amps, ohms or continuity, depending on the dial setting.

parts.label: Selector dial
parts.body: Chooses what you're measuring: AC/DC voltage, current, resistance or continuity.

parts.label: Test probes
parts.body: Red (positive) and black (negative) leads touch the circuit to take a reading.

quiz.q: Which of these can a multimeter measure?
Why test with a multimeter before working on a circuit?
options: To prove the circuit is safely dead
Whether a wire path is complete and unbroken

tools.name: Insulated Screwdriver
tools.short: VDE-rated insulation protects against shock near live parts.
tools.what: An insulated screwdriver is rated (commonly VDE 1000V) with insulation built into the handle and shaft to protect against electric shock when working near live parts.
tools.usage: Electricians use VDE-rated tools whenever there's a risk of contact with a live conductor — extra protection layered on top of safe isolation procedures, never a replacement for them.

parts.label: Insulated handle
parts.body: Moulded, tested insulation rated to a specific voltage (commonly 1000V) — the tool's main safety feature.

parts.label: Insulated shaft
parts.body: Unlike a standard screwdriver, the metal shaft itself is coated in insulation, right up to the tip.

parts.label: Tip
parts.body: Only the very tip is bare metal, sized to fit the screw head precisely and avoid slipping.

quiz.q: What does "VDE rated" mean for a screwdriver?
options: It's tested and insulated for use near live electrical parts
Instead of switching off the power
As extra protection alongside safe isolation

quiz.q: What should you check before using one?
options: The handle colour matches your van
The insulation isn't damaged or worn
It's the most expensive one available

trades.name: Plumbing
trades.tagline: Keeping water, waste and gas systems flowing safely.

tools.name: Pipe Wrench
tools.short: Grips and turns round pipe and fittings without crushing them.
tools.what: A pipe wrench has serrated, self-tightening jaws — one fixed hook jaw and one adjustable jaw set with a knurled nut. The more force you apply, the harder the jaws bite into the pipe.
tools.usage: Plumbers use it to grip and turn round pipe and fittings without crushing or slipping — essential for assembling or removing threaded steel and iron pipework.

parts.label: Hook jaw
parts.body: The fixed, curved jaw. It hooks onto the pipe while the adjustable jaw clamps from the other side.

parts.label: Adjusting nut
parts.body: A knurled nut that winds the lower jaw up or down, setting the size of the bite for different pipe diameters.

parts.label: Handle
parts.body: A long handle gives leverage — the harder you pull, the tighter the serrated jaws grip the pipe.

quiz.q: What makes a pipe wrench different from a normal spanner?
options: It has smooth jaws for delicate work
Its serrated jaws bite harder under load

quiz.q: What is a pipe wrench mainly designed to grip?
What adjusts the size of a pipe wrench's jaw opening?

tools.name: Adjustable Spanner
tools.short: One tool, many sizes — a moving jaw set by a worm screw.
tools.what: An adjustable spanner (wrench) has one fixed jaw and one moving jaw, set by turning a worm screw. That lets a single tool fit many different nut and bolt sizes.
tools.usage: Plumbers reach for it on compression fittings, tap connectors and nuts where an exact-size spanner isn't to hand — a genuine multi-size tool for the toolbox.

parts.label: Jaws
parts.body: One jaw is fixed to the head, the other slides to grip nuts and fittings of different widths.

parts.label: Worm screw
parts.body: Turning this knurled wheel moves the sliding jaw in or out to fit the fitting exactly.

parts.label: Handle
parts.body: A flat steel handle that gives good leverage for turning nuts and fittings.

quiz.q: What lets an adjustable spanner fit different sized nuts?
options: A worm screw that moves one jaw

quiz.q: To avoid rounding off a nut, which way should you pull?
options: Pull toward you so the fixed jaw takes the load

quiz.q: Adjustable spanners are especially useful for:
options: Tasks needing one exact fixed size only
A range of nut and bolt sizes on the job

tools.name: Plunger
tools.short: A sealed rubber cup that forces pressure through a blocked pipe.
tools.what: A plunger uses a flexible rubber cup to form a seal, then pushes and pulls water to force air and pressure through a pipe and shift a blockage.
tools.usage: Plumbers use it as the first, simplest tool for clearing blocked toilets, sinks and drains before reaching for rods, augers or chemical cleaners.

parts.label: Rubber cup
parts.body: The flexible cup forms an airtight seal over the drain opening so pressure can build up.

parts.label: Handle
parts.body: A long handle lets you pump the cup up and down with steady, controlled force.

parts.label: Ferrule
parts.body: The metal collar joining handle to cup, keeping the two firmly fixed together.

quiz.q: What does a plunger rely on to clear a blockage?
options: A sealed cup pushing air/water pressure through the pipe

quiz.q: What is essential for a plunger to work well?
options: A good seal over the opening
The last resort after cutting the pipe
The first, simplest tool to try on a blockage
Only used for testing water pressure
